findings.claim: Both observations are true because they describe different match modes: the track rules say practice house bots act as one squad and never fight each other, while the 62-of-65 house-on-house kills were measured in public play.joinbuilders.org matches (humans plus house bots). Nothing in the kit says the two modes share house-bot behavior. Public-match infighting is therefore no evidence about practice, and practice placement points come only from our kills and house zone deaths.

sources.quote: acting as one squad: they share vision, never fight each other
62 of 65 house-bot deaths were kills by other house bots ... MEASURED (public matches only. Practice house config is unverified.)
played in 48 practice matches against built-in bots

findings.suggested_change: For practice and qualifying-for-top-32 work, plan on fighting: take winnable 1v1s against the early lone hunters and finish wounded targets (EV-R-0020..0023). Don't tune hiding or outlasting on practice. Revisit hiding only for the final, where the track page says the qualifying round and the series are 16-mech free-for-alls between team bots, which do kill each other.
findings.mechanism: If no house bot ever kills another, a 48-match practice score of 2.38 means about 2.4 squad deaths before ours, from our kills or the zone. Hiding only delays our death against a squad that shares vision and adds hunters over time, so it cannot add places. Kills add places directly and drop cubes.

failure_classes.basis: practice rules: placement only from our kills and zone deaths; the bot flees at 35% of its own HP regardless of the enemy
